summary.text:
A combined authority with an unusually clean balance sheet: MCA holds £544m of investments against £39m of external PWLB debt, and the Police Fund carries £12.2m of investments against £27m of PWLB. Combined external debt is £66m across 25 PWLB loans, and our file ties loan-by-loan to their Table 9 -- MCA 7 loans / £39.0m at 4.96% weighted (rate range 4.25%-5.88% matches their stated 4.25%-5.875%), Police Fund 18 loans / £26,984,000 at 4.34% weighted (ties to Table 9 total £27,784k less the £800k matured during 2025/26).

The balance-sheet identity closes to the pound on both sides: MCA CFR £116m less £39m external less £13m OLTL = £64m internal borrowing (their stated -£64m); Police Fund CFR £154m less £27m less £2m = £125m (their stated -£125m). MCA is 62% internally funded; Police Fund 83%. That is about to change on the Police side: the paper flags £135m of new external borrowing needed across 2026/27-2028/29 (£49m + £55m + £31m) as the reserves cover runs down, and it explicitly names intra-divisional borrowing from MCA cash as one of the three options alongside the LA market and PWLB.

The paper's own hook is at p.10: one £5m loan is 'below the prevailing rate for the prepayment of debt' and officers are 'looking into the financial benefit of repaying this debt early'. That loan is identifiable from our file as PW493047, £5m at 4.25% maturing 2052 -- our engine sizes the indicative discount at £883k on the 14 August DMO curve. The MCA book overall carries an indicative net discount of £489k (1.3% of principal), with six other loans at premiums. The maturity profile also has a concentration in 2027/28 (£22m, 52% of the MCA book), split between two 4.88% loans that would refinance close to their current coupon on the MUFG forecast and two 5.88% loans that would refinance below it.

The MUFG rate forecast (dated 25 March 2026) is testable and dated: 5-year PWLB 5.00% Jun-26 falling to 4.10% Mar-29, Bank Rate held at 3.75% through Mar-27. The paper honestly flags an internal tension at p.5 -- the market is now pricing 'between 1 and 2 interest rate rises this financial year', the opposite direction from MUFG's held-then-cut path. On 14 August fixings the long end sits about 0.35-0.5 percentage points above MUFG's March reference, so the market has already moved against the adviser view.

officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more -- the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief -- in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on your 2025/26 Treasury Outturn -- the Appendix E that went to the Board on 14 July. You're not being singled out -- every authority gets one of these -- and there's no agenda in it. It's a well-structured report that separates MCA and Police cleanly and rebuilds against the balance sheet, and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

As a cross-check our figures tie to yours on both sides. On the MCA book we hold 7 PWLB loans totalling £39,000,000 at a weighted 4.96%, which matches your Table 8 £39m and your Table 9 buckets loan-by-loan -- and the rate range you cite at p.10, 4.25% to 5.875%, matches ours to the second decimal. On the Police Fund book we hold 18 loans totalling £26,984,000 at a weighted 4.34%, which is your Table 9 total of £27,784k less the £800k that matured during 2025/26. Loan-level view is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis if you want to see it.

Paragraph 10 flagged a £5m loan sitting below the prevailing repayment rate that officers are looking at. From our file that reads across to your 4.25% 2052 maturity, and on the DMO's repayment curve at 14 August (notice 314/26 PM) our engine sizes the indicative discount at about £883k, roughly 17.7% of principal. Six of your other MCA loans price at small premiums, so the whole-book indicative discount nets to about £489k -- meaningful, but concentrated in that one 2052 loan. Only the DMO can give a binding quote and we don't model MRP or the accounting treatment; whether it's worth doing turns on replacement cost you'd carry which we don't model. But the arithmetic is knowable and the loan is the one your paper points to.

One other observation on maturity shape. On the MCA book £22m falls in 2027/28 -- 52% of the £39m -- split between two 4.88% loans and one 5.88% loan (plus a smaller 5.88% maturing March 2027). On the MUFG forecast in your Table 5 the 5-year PWLB drops from 5.00% Jun-26 to 4.20% Mar-28, so the 4.88% pair would refinance close to their current coupon and the 5.88% pair well below it. Worth noting alongside that: your Table 5 is dated 25 March, and on the 14 August fixings the long end is running about 0.3 to 0.5 percentage points above MUFG's Jun-26 reference. The paper itself flags the internal tension at p.5 -- markets are pricing in one to two rate rises this year rather than the held-then-cut path in the forecast. Live PWLB fixings are at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard.

There's a wider point that's rare in the papers we read. The MCA sits on £544m of investments against £39m of external debt -- that's a 62% under-borrowed position on your side -- while the Police Fund faces £135m of new external borrowing across 2026/27 to 2028/29 as its own reserve cover runs off. The paper explicitly names intra-divisional borrowing between the Police Fund and the MCA as one of the three options at p.6, alongside the LA-to-LA market and PWLB. That's a much cleaner internal transfer than most authorities have available, and the intra-LA market data at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity gives you the external benchmark for pricing it.

On training, four look most relevant. PWLB early repayment -- when discounts make sense speaks directly to the 4.25% 2052 loan work. Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets covers pricing on the Police intra-divisional route. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice fits the under-borrowed position and its planned unwind. Interest rate risk maps to the 2027/28 concentration. Our liability benchmark pathway is interactive and built on live data, which is likely to matter given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free -- https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn -- https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
